# AI-Rulez

> Author, generate, validate and govern AI agent rules, skills, plugins and MCP configuration across 52 coding assistants. Review with verified model evidence, evaluate skills, lock and sign dependencies, and publish bundles. CLI, MCP server and Go API.

## Docs

- [Home](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/): AI-Rulez keeps the instructions for your AI coding assistants in one place, .ai-rulez/, and generates the native files of 52 assistants from it.

## Get started

- [Installation](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installation/): ai-rulez is a single binary, distributed through Homebrew, npm, PyPI and Go.
- [Quick start](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/quick-start/): Set up ai-rulez in a repository, add a rule, and generate the files for five assistants.
- [Examples](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/examples/): Complete configurations for common setups.
- [Migrating to v5](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/migration-v5/): Upgrade a 4.x project to ai-rulez 5.

## Author

- [Configuration](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/configuration/): .ai-rulez/config.toml declares which tools ai-rulez generates for, which content each profile selects, and how the generated files look.
- [Rules](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/rules/): A rule is one markdown file in .ai-rulez/rules/ (or .ai-rulez/domains/\<domain\>/rules/) with instructions the assistant should follow.
- [Skills](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/skills/): A skill is a directory .ai-rulez/skills/\<id\>/ (or .ai-rulez/domains/\<domain\>/skills/\<id\>/) with a SKILL.md: YAML frontmatter followed by the instructions, plus optional references/, scripts/ and...
- [Checks](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/checks/): A check is a code-review guideline: one topic a review tool (Cursor Bugbot, Kilo Code Reviews, GitLab Duo, Augment, Amp, ...) applies to every pull or merge request.
- [OKF (Open Knowledge Format)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/okf/): OKF is a directory of markdown files with YAML frontmatter, meant to be read by people and by agents.
- [Domains and profiles](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/domains/): A domain is a named folder of content (.ai-rulez/domains/\<name\>/) for one team, service or area of the project.
- [Roles](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/roles/): A role maps a job to the slice of the shared content a person needs: which domains, which skills, rules, agents, commands and checks, and how each skill is surfaced.
- [Includes](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/includes/): An include pulls rules, context, skills, agents, commands and checks from another directory or git repository into your project, so an organization's standards are written once and shared by many...
- [Installed skills](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installed-skills/): An \[\[installedskills\]\] entry pulls one or more Agent Skills from a git repository or a local directory and writes them into every harness's skills folder, as if they were your own.
- [Installed plugins](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installed-plugins/): Import a harness plugin (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI or Agent Plugins) and render its skills, agents, commands, rules, hooks and MCP servers into every preset you generate.
- [.agents as a source](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agents-source/): With source = "agents", ai-rulez reads your content from the open standards (the root AGENTS.md and the .agents/ directory) instead of .ai-rulez/, and generates every other tool's files from them.
- [Config without a .ai-rulez folder](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/config-without-folder/): Keep the whole ai-rulez configuration in one file, ai-rulez.toml at the project root, with no .ai-rulez/ directory.
- [Local configuration](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/local-overrides/): Machine-local configuration that is never committed: scratch notes, per-machine paths, personal presets and MCP servers, secrets and experiments that belong to your checkout but not to the shared...
- [Catalog](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/catalog/): ai-rulez catalog lists everything a project defines (rules, context, skills, agents, commands and checks) with owner, version, token cost, lock digest, the roles that keep each item and its lint...
- [Monorepos](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/monorepo/): A large repository needs each agent to see the instructions for the code it is working on, and not much more.

## Generate

- [Supported harnesses](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/harnesses/): ai-rulez has 52 built-in presets, one per AI coding harness.
- [Custom presets](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/profiles/): presets in .ai-rulez/config.toml lists the tools ai-rulez generates for.
- [AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agents-md/): AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/ are the cross-tool conventions for project instructions and Agent Skills.
- [Managing only remote skills](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/managing-remote-skills/): Use this setup when you write CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and your own skills by hand and want ai-rulez to manage only the parts that come from elsewhere: installed skills, plugins, MCP servers, hooks...
- [llms.txt](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/llms-txt/): llms.txt is a Markdown index at the root of a site or repository that tells language models what is there and where to read it.
- [Hooks and settings](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/settings/): ai-rulez generate writes lifecycle hooks, the generated-file guard and a few other settings keys into each harness's native settings file, from one declaration in config.toml.
- [Permissions](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/permissions/): \[permissions\] is one allow / ask / deny list for every harness that has a native permission file.
- [Run generate in remote sessions](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/session-start/): A remote (cloud) agent session starts from a fresh clone of the repository.
- [User-level configuration](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/user-scope/): ai-rulez generate --user renders a personal configuration into the per-user directories each harness reads (~/.claude, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, ~/.config/opencode, ~/.copilot...
- [Baz](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/baz/): The baz preset writes the files the Baz pull request reviewer reads from a repository.

## Bundle and publish

- [Authoring plugins](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/plugins/): ai-rulez generate --plugin packages the skills, commands, agents, MCP servers and hooks of your .ai-rulez/ project as installable plugin bundles for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Kimi...
- [Agent Plugins](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agent-plugins/): The agent-plugins plugin runtime packages your skills and MCP servers as an Agent Plugins directory: a root plugin.json, a skills/ tree and an mcp.json, which any client that implements the...
- [Agentic Resource Discovery](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/ard/): The ard emitter publishes your skills, remote MCP servers and plugin for discovery through Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD): one ard.json manifest that registries and agents fetch from...
- [MCP server cards](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/mcp-server-card/): The mcp-server-card emitter writes an MCP Server Card (SEP-2127) for each remote MCP server of your project.
- [Publish](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/publish/): ai-rulez publish turns the generated plugin bundle into release artifacts: a reproducible tar.gz, a manifest, checksums, release notes and a plan.

## Validate

- [Strict validation](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/strict-validation/): ai-rulez validate checks that the configuration loads and matches the schema, then lints the content: globs that select nothing, links and references that point nowhere, hooks that cannot run...
- [Harness traps](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/harness-traps/): Some harnesses accept a file that looks valid and then silently ignore it: a rule in .cursor/rules/x.md is never read, and a Copilot instructions file named go.md is skipped.
- [Verifiers](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/verifiers/): Verifiers are read-only checks over the repository that back up what your rules and skills say: a file exists, no TODO( is left in shipped code, package.json pins the Node version a rule mentions...
- [Session exposure and areas](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/exposure/): In a large repository, every session starts with the same context: the root instruction file, the unconditional rules, the listing of root skills and agents, and the MCP server names.
- [GitHub Actions](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/github-actions/): ai-rulez ships three composite actions:
- [Poly hooks](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/poly-hooks/): ai-rulez publishes a hook catalog for Poly, poly-hooks.toml at the root of its repository.

## Govern

- [Trust model](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/trust-model/): A repository's .ai-rulez/ directory is content someone else may have written.
- [Lock file](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/lockfile/): ai-rulez.lock records exactly what your AI configuration is made of: every remote source by commit and digest, every authored rule, skill, hook and role by content digest, and every generated file...
- [Approvals](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/approvals/): A scan says content looks clean; an approval records that a named person read it and accepted it.
- [Signing](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/signing/): A digest proves that bytes did not change; a signature says who produced them.
- [Organization policy](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/policy/): An organization policy is a floor a repository may raise but never lower.
- [SBOM](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/sbom/): ai-rulez sbom writes a bill of materials of your AI configuration as CycloneDX 1.6 or SPDX 2.3 JSON: every rule, skill, hook and agent, every remote source and MCP server, with digests, pins and...
- [Forge client](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/forge/): Some governance features ask GitHub a question: when was this tag released, who approved this pull request, who is in this team.

## Operate

- [MCP server](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/mcp-server/): ai-rulez mcp is a Model Context Protocol server that lets your coding assistant read, edit, validate and generate your .ai-rulez/ configuration, and serve skills and nested repository context on...
- [Skill search](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/search/): ai-rulez search ranks your project's skills against a query with the same ranker the MCP findskill tool uses, and search --eval measures that ranking against labeled queries.
- [Usage telemetry](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/usage-telemetry/): Usage telemetry tells you which skills your team's agents actually use, which ones were edited since they were last used, and which ones never fire and can be retired.
- [Item-load telemetry (OTLP)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/telemetry/): Item-load telemetry records which rules, agents and context files a harness actually loaded, so you can see how many rules a session carries and which ones never load.
- [Evals](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/evals/): Evals check that a skill fires when it should, stays quiet when it should not, and does the job when it fires.
- [Improve (experimental)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/improve/): ai-rulez improve run \<skill\> --with CMD runs an optimizer (a program that rewrites a skill) on a throwaway copy of the skill and keeps its candidate only if the skill does measurably better on...
- [Review](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/review/): ai-rulez review scores your skills, agents and commands against a rubric: is the trigger concrete, does the description overlap a sibling, does the body match what it promises.
- [Judge](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/judge/): ai-rulez judge audits agent configuration with language models and reports security, governance and quality findings.
- [LLM access](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/llm/): The \[llm\] table configures the one model connection every model-backed ai-rulez feature shares: the provider and model, the spend caps, the response cache and the privacy rules.
- [Performance](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/performance/): What the common ai-rulez operations cost on a typical project, which settings change that, and how a slowdown in ai-rulez itself is caught before release.

## Reference

- [Architecture](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/architecture/): How ai-rulez turns a source tree into the native files of 52 assistants, and where each step lives in the code.
- [Standards conformance](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/standards/): ai-rulez writes several open formats besides each assistant's native files.
- [CLI guide](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/cli/): ai-rulez turns one .ai-rulez/ source tree into the instruction files, rules, skills, MCP configuration, hooks and permissions of every coding assistant you list in presets.
- [CLI command reference](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/cli-reference/): Every command, with its usage, aliases, examples and flags, generated from the binary's own command tree.
- [Schema](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/schema/): ai-rulez publishes JSON Schemas for its configuration file and for every JSON document its commands print.
- [Embedding (Go API)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/embedding/): The package github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5/pkg/airulez runs the ai-rulez engine from Go: load a project, validate it, plan or apply a generate run, and write or check its lock.
- [Architecture decision records](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/adr-index/): Repository decisions use MADR in adrs/.
